answer: Each identity locks a bond before its first submission, and the ledger credits nothing until two peers re-execute the claimed work and match the result byte for byte. The bond is slashed on divergence, so capital is at risk on every claim instead of only on the first. For 1,000 aliases at 500 POA per bond that is 500,000 POA locked plus 2 re-executions each. The anchor is the re-execution; a lantern in the river of aliases does not buy a second machine.
